    #147964. Brands race to systematize how to know what makes creator content worth paying for

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (906 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Digiday ↗ Open Full Page

    Brands race to systematize how to know what makes creator content worth paying for

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Digiday

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, join us Dec.
    • Social media trends move faster than brands can keep up with.
    • It has been revealed that take General Mills, for example.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, join us Dec. 1-3 in Nashville for the Digiday Programmatic Marketing Summit.

    Social media trends move faster than brands can keep up with. Now, they’re trying to create repeatable systems to turn organic social attention into something they can evaluate, fund and ultimately scale.

    It has been revealed that take General Mills, for example. Home to brands like Cheerios, Cinnamon Toast Crunch and Trix, the CPG brand has spent the past year putting together an internal framework to systematize monetizing viral moments.

    In a recent development, its “talkability score” is a calculation used to measure whether General Mills’ brands are earning more attention with social media creators than they’re buying with paid ads. It’s a loose framework that varies by brand, Mindy Murray, director of influencer and content at General Mills said, and generates a score based on whether users shared it, put their own spin on it and how long interest in the trend lasts.

    Recent findings suggest that murray was mum on the actual mechanics on how it actually determines whether to invest ad spend. “We’re weighing on earning, we’re weighing things like active engagement — so shares likes, comments, saves — because we know that that means someone took an actual effort to do something versus just an impression,” Murray said.

    Virality can’t be manufactured, but this “operating system” allows them to “go faster and be smarter,” mentioned Murray.

    Over the past year, General Mills has also reorganized its teams to bring social and influencer marketing under Murray’s purview, she told Digiday, to move more promptly and efficiently in converting buzzy organic content into paid ads.

    For example, over the summer Reese’s “Eat ‘Em Up” cereal jingle from the early 2000s started trending on TikTok. General Mills noticed the trend, partnered with GloRilla to re-record the rap, tracked real-time activity via its framework, and ultimately turned it into a campaign on streaming platforms and Reese’s Puffs’ YouTube channel. The company boasted a 2.5% year-over-year sales increase as a result, but did not provide specific sales figures. The company did not say specifically how the framework informed that strategy.

    Last week, influencer agency Billion Dollar Boy (BDB) rolled out its Creator Investment Planner, a financial modeling tool that aims to help marketers understand the ad spend levels required to strategy and “de-risk creator investments,” according to a news release.

    BDB’s tool works by calculating blended CPMs from creators and social media platforms. Marketers enter their budget and time frame, and the platform calculates estimates for share of voice, total impressions and earned media value. Per BDB, the model can upgrade as inputs change, where marketers can expect to “de-risk” spend commitments.

    And in April, CreatorIQ creator platform and creative analytics and governance platform CreativeX launched a new tool to help brands incorporate creator content into a paid media strategy. The system works on an API, sending creator content from CreatorIQ’s platform to CreativeX to be graded, reviewed by CreativeX’s AI-powered system and optimized by a brand campaign manager. Ultimately, it aims to identify creator posts with potential to do well as an ad before any media buyers open their wallets. Nestlé was the first brand to sign on. The integration was declared on an invite-only basis.

    To agency execs, all signs point to brands getting more rigorous about their spend — especially when it comes to squeezing performance out of creators — and do it before the trend disappears.

    According to recent reports, creator spend is expected to increase 12% every year until 2030, according to advertising research firm Madison & Wall. In no small part, brand spend on boosting or promoting creator content is fueling that growth.

    “Before any sort of budget is unlocked, you have to be able to prove out that there’s a higher propensity for that piece of content for whatever investment you’re making into social to actually move towards a conversion,” stated Madison Gaudry-Routledge, evp of social at Viral Nation, a social agency.

    Most brands, Gaudry-Routledge said, haven’t come up with a named framework in the same way General Mills has. Brand spend on creator marketing is expected to grow twice as fast as spending on advertising. Naturally, brands are eager to see proof of concept as early as possible.

    In a recent development, viral Nation has its own proprietary framework offered to clients as an add-on service. It’s called Culture Quotient that blends brand awareness, brand affinity and brand velocity into a measurable score to determine a brand’s relevance in cultural conversation. The tool works via AI that analyzes conversations and content, identifies emerging cultural trends and tracks shifts in consumer sentiment, per Gaudry-Routledge. The social exec declined to share any client-specific examples.

    These calculations are being built in real time and haven’t yet replaced traditional metrics like share of voice, audience sentiment and engagement.

    “As an industry, we’re continuing to try to catch up on operationalizing frameworks and systematizing measurement and still not there yet,” said Kristina Coughlin, svp and general manager of Trevant, a creator marketing agency.

    Dick’s is betting that youth sports can fuel its next phase of ad growth through GameChanger—if it can overcome limits on scale.

    As Black Friday Cyber Monday rapidly approaches, brands are most focused on acquiring newly introduced customers this holiday season.

    Product discovery habits are changing, leaving marketers unsure how to pivot ahead of the biggest sales period of the year.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    While retailers have been developing agents that can shop on behalf of customers, Target’s newly introduced shopping assistant is not that—yet.

    In October, Target rolled out a beta version of its AI assistant, Ask Target, within its website and mobile app. The assistant finds items based on shopper preferences, shares product facts, compares items, summarizes reviews, and checks inventory availability.

    “We really are taking a phased approach in terms of AI and the types of problems it’s going to solve for our guests,” Purvi Shah, svp of user experience at Target, told ADWEEK.

    Ask Target is now available to all shoppers after initially testing the feature with Target employees.

    • CMC is the most referenced price and market data source in crypto.
    • Sources indicate that you will own our research agenda end to end: what we publish, how rigorous it is, and how it supports our enterprise data business.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that coinMarketCap is hiring a Head of Research to turn CMC data into research that institutions, media and partners trust and pay for. This is a senior, hands-on role reporting to the CMO.

    CMC is the most referenced price and market data source in crypto. Our research already reaches millions each month through reports like our Monthly Exchange Report, Asset Watch and Market Pulse, and is cited by Bloomberg, WSJ, Forbes and Fortune. The next step is different. We are building CMC into a data platform for crypto, tokenized assets and broader markets, and research is how we prove the quality of that data to the people who buy it.

    Sources indicate that you will own our research agenda end to end: what we publish, how rigorous it is, and how it supports our enterprise data business. You will also be the senior voice on sensitive market analysis for CMC and its partners.

    Set and run the research roadmap, from recurring flagships (monthly exchange report, weekly market and asset coverage) to deep dives on exchanges, tokenized assets, RWAs and market structure.

    Build institutional grade research that showcases CMC data to banks, funds, data buyers and enterprise API clients, working closely with our API and BD teams on what buyers need.

    Own methodology and data integrity: define how we measure volume, liquidity, flows and reserves, document it, and make sure every published number holds up to scrutiny.

    Lead research on sensitive or fast moving market events, balancing speed, neutrality and accuracy, and handle review requests from partners with sound judgement.

    Be a credible public face for CMC research with tier one media, on panels and in interviews.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    AI can raise the ceiling on marketing, or it can expose every weak foundation underneath it.

    Live from the Marketing Vanguard stage at Brandweek 2026, Jenny Rooney sits down with Laura Knebusch, senior vice president of CPG marketing and customer experience at Georgia-Pacific, to explore what modern brand building really requires when media, data, retail, and AI are all evolving at once.

    Laura gets into why Georgia-Pacific spent 18 months consolidating data sources, and how that foundation now supports in-house capabilities and agentic AI.

    She also discusses why consumer-first and AI-first marketing are not actually competing ideas.

    This episode is part of a special vidcast series that was recorded live during Brandweek 2026 and presented in partnership with Tatari.

    Laura Knebusch is Senior Vice President of CPG Marketing and Customer Experience at Georgia-Pacific, where her team supports consumer and B2B brands across insights, content, media, promotions, marketing technology and analytics.

    She began her marketing career at Procter & Gamble after earning her MBA from Duke and later joined Georgia-Pacific, where she has spent 18 years across brand management, category leadership and marketing capability roles.

    Today, her focus is on combining classic brand-building fundamentals with the data, technology and operating models needed for modern CPG marketing.

    It has been revealed that private Label Is Waiting, So What About Your Brand? — Laura points out that consumers have been adjusting their behavior for years, not reacting to one sudden economic moment. In household essentials, private-label options are credible and easy to access. There’s a warning lying there for marketers: if the brand does not create a real reason to choose it, loyalty becomes much harder to defend.

    According to recent reports, 100 Data Sources, One Source of Truth, Eighteen Months of Work — When Laura stepped into her current role, Georgia-Pacific needed to become more digitally capable. The first step was not another tool. It was fixing the data. Over 18 months, the team connected roughly 100 different sources, cleaned and harmonized them, and built one accessible system that now powers multiple in-house capabilities.

    Sources indicate that consumer-First vs. AI-First Is the Wrong Debate — At Brandweek 2026, Laura describes an internal discussion that paired behavioral science with generative-engine optimization. At first, the advice sounded different – Humans need simplicity, distinctiveness and repetition, while AI needs clear, consistent information. But the conclusion was the same: strong fundamentals work for both.

    Sources indicate that why Georgia-Pacific Merged Shopper Marketing and National Media — Retail media has changed how consumers discover and buy, so Georgia-Pacific changed how it organizes around that reality. Laura explains why shopper marketing and national media were brought closer together, helping the team better understand where partners create strategic value and where investment should stay tactical.

    Jenny Rooney is Chief Brand and Community Officer, leading strategy for the overall ADWEEK brand as well as the ways in which we serve and support our audiences with high-value content, products, partnerships and experiences, notably through our community programs such as Marketing Vanguard.

    According to recent reports, we are hiring 2026 and 2027 Graduate Software Engineers into engineering teams around the world. We work from the very lowest levels of the Linux system - BIOS and boot loaders, firmware, kernel and drivers, all the way up to desktop applications and containers. We work on compilers and toolchains, and we work on security, cryptography, performance and documentation. Some of our teams focus on packaging thousands of pieces of software, others focus on deep contributions to a single body of code.

The process is highly competitive, it will require effort and excellence to succeed if you apply here.

    Industry observers note that most of our engineering teams work from home. We try to align a single team in a single time zone - EMEA (Europe, Middle East and Africa), APAC (Asia Pacific and Indian Ocean), and AMER (North, South and Central Americas). Even though you work from home, we try to ensure you always have colleagues alongside to coach and mentor you, and for the companionship of shared problem solving and pair programming. Larger projects have multiple teams and might span the globe. We work with the open source community and specialize in building teams that work well in the 'fishbowl' of open source engineering. This is full time work, five days a week, often solving hard problems with significant responsibility. We don't generally work weekends and nights and we do enjoy good holidays but we also expect productive and intense engagement Monday to Friday.

    According to recent reports, we bring all our engineering teams together in person twice a year for a deep 'sprint' with other teams to stimulate discussion and enable a wide range of career development paths. This is a fantastic way to demonstrate and develop your skill in software, learn about a wide range of technologies, make a meaningful impact to open source, and see some very interesting new cities that you might never otherwise get to visit.

    If you find the open source stack amazing, and you have been a consistent high-performing student in your school and university, then this will be a challenging and exciting start to your career.

    Tech Report: AI Native Creative Strategist - EdTech (French fluent 🇫🇷) at Paradox

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • What if your next playground was to build a global, iconic Brand, with a creative machine that never sleeps, and compounds?
    • We’re not looking for a "Social Media Manager" to follow a calendar.
    • Someone who understands that to win today, you don’t just need "content", you need a Movement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    What if your next playground was to build a global, iconic Brand, with a creative machine that never sleeps, and compounds?

    We’re not looking for a "Social Media Manager" to follow a calendar. We’re looking for an AI-native Creative Strategist (Brand & Content).

    Someone who understands that to win today, you don’t just need "content", you need a Movement.

    This isn’t another content job. Most content teams use AI to write captions faster. That’s the 99%. We want to be in the 0.1%: a media where AI runs the creative loop, from the signal to the hook, the cut, the post and the lesson. Every day, on every platform, in French and in English. You bring the taste. The machine you build brings the scale.

    Here’s the bet: a organization that learns by itself grows in a way a company of people alone can’t. We aim for $10M in revenue with 10 people, each of them running a dozen agents.

    Paradoxically, the more AI runs our content, the more human it has to feel. AI doesn’t make more of what everyone makes. It makes more of what only we can make.

    Our creative machine has to be able to:.

    In a recent development, 1. Read the signals. Comments, DMs, retention graphs, saves, shares, search trends, objections from sales calls, and what the best creators and advertisers in the world are publishing right now.

    It has been revealed that 2. Hold the full context of Paradox. Our DNA, years of interviews, lives and courses, member stories, and every past post with what it taught us, in one shared company brain.

    3. Generate in our voice. Hooks, scripts, shorts, carousels, cuts, thumbnails and captions, in French and in English.

    4. Ship. Format, schedule, publish and answer, on every platform.

    It has been revealed that 5. Measure with real KPIs. Retention, shares, saves, follower growth, and the followers who become leads and members. Not likes.

    Sources indicate that 6. Learn and loop on its own. Double down on what works, kill what doesn’t, write the lesson back into the brain, and start the next cycle without waiting for a meeting.

    This is already real. An ads library of thousands of creatives feeds our creative research. Agents cut ads from long-form content and wire Instagram comment-to-DM automations. And our product is AI-native too: Athena, our AI coach, works with members every day.

    At Paradox, we are convinced that greatness is trainable, and we believe self-help is broken.

    Most learning platforms are used the same way: consuming generic theories, getting quick highs, ending with no real change.

    People deserve more: a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges, and grows with them.

    That’s why we want to empower people at scale, by leveraging cutting edge technologies like AI, and crafting user experiences with outstanding aesthetics.

    - Human Intelligence (coaches, peers, and mentors).

    - Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals).

    - Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys).

    To create one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS.

    It has been revealed that paradox was founded by David Laroche, a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson and Gad Elmaleh. We started in French. We’re building for the world.

    You lead the Content Factory not by management, but with creativity.

    Recent findings suggest that in a classic content team, people do the work and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the volume, you design the machine, set the bar and make the calls. Humans do what no machine can: taste.

    Build a symbiotic strategy where David Laroche’s personal brand and Paradox’s company brand reinforce each other without cannibalization.

    Implement radical new formats (documentaries, conceptual shorts) that shatter the boring codes of the "Self-Help" industry.

    Define distinct, sharp editorial lines for each platform: Depth & Search for YouTube, Aesthetic & Vibe for Instagram, and Authority & Authenticity for LinkedIn.

    ❌ The old way: a strategy deck written once a year, and a calendar filled by habit.

    It has been revealed that 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: agents watch every platform, every competitor and every comment continuously. They tell you which angle is rising, which format is tiring and which story our audience asks for. The strategy updates every week, on evidence.

    Take responsibility for the entire production chain from hooks to storyboarding the narrative, and ensuring the final cut matches the vision.

    Recent findings suggest that own the packaging: titles, thumbnails and the first 3 seconds. You test variants every week and know your click-through and retention numbers by heart.

    ❌ The old way: one shoot becomes one video and a handful of posts.

    In a recent development, 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: one shoot, one live or one interview becomes dozens of hooks, shorts, carousels and ad cuts by the next morning, in both languages. Concepts are tested with AI-generated drafts before we spend a day shooting them.

    It has been revealed that your taste becomes the eval. You write down what makes a great hook, a great cut, a great carousel and a great story, in rules and examples the agents check themselves against. Each time you reject something, the reason goes back into the rules.

    Act as the final quality check: nothing gets published if it doesn’t meet the "Paradox Standard" of aesthetics and storytelling, whether a person or an agent made it.

    ❌ The old way: a creative team briefs an editor, waits three days and gets two versions.

    In a recent development, 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: agents draft, cut, caption, translate and schedule. You keep the best, and next week their first drafts are already closer to your bar.

    Analyze retention graphs, CTR, and CPL to iterate based on feedback, killing what fails and aggressively scaling what works.

    ❌ The old way: someone pulls the stats at the end of the month and nobody changes anything.

    In a recent development, 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: agents read the numbers of every post every day, explain why it worked or didn’t, and propose the next test. You measure the machine itself: posts per week, time from idea to live, hit rate, and the share of the work done without a human.

    Recent findings suggest that we started in French. You build the machine that takes Paradox to English-speaking audiences: channels, formats and voice that feel native, not translated.

    It has been revealed that and always: real stories told with consent, no fake claims, no fake scarcity. The machine can scale, but it doesn’t decide what’s right. You do.

    How you’ll know you’re AI-native: you spend your time on concepts, taste and calls, not on resizing, captioning and exporting. The output grows every month while the team doesn’t.

    In a recent development, proven Content Builder: You have successfully grown a media brand, a YouTube channel, or a personal brand to significant scale (100k+ followers or millions of views). You understand the mechanics of virality and retention. You’ve created at least one format that broke out, and you can show its click-through and retention numbers.

    Elite Scripting Skills: You can show us scripts you wrote that performed. You know how to structure a narrative, write a hook that stops the scroll, and keep an audience engaged for 20+ minutes.

    Performance Fluency: You have worked in environments where content had to drive business results (ads, launches, conversion), not just vanity metrics.

    In a recent development, AI-native Creative: you’ve built content pipelines with AI yourself: Claude Code, automations, generative video, image and voice tools, evals. Show us something you built, not a certificate.

    According to recent reports, intolerant to Mediocrity: You have "Taste." You are physically pained by a bad font, a clumsy cut, or a weak headline. You fight for the details that others ignore, including in what AI produces.

    It has been revealed that psychology Obsessed: You don’t just "make content"; you study human nature. You constantly ask why people click, why they share, and what emotion drives them.

    A "Doer" with Authority: You command respect not by title, but by competence. You can jump into a project, write the script, direct the shoot, and fix the edit if needed.

    Loop thinker: you see every platform as a loop that can learn, and you can’t stop yourself from closing it.

    No Ego, Just Impact: You don’t fall in love with your ideas. You accept that even the best concepts can flop. When it happens, you don’t take it personally; you analyze the data, pivot immediately, and ship the next concept with renewed energy.

    English: Fluent English, you can hold a conversation on specific details with English-speaking colleagues.

    Our chosen language for written communication is English.

    ❌ If you need clarity before chaos: wrong place.

    ❌ If you prefer balance over intensity: wrong season.

    ❌ If you don’t genuinely care about the topics we cover: wrong place.

    ❌ If you want to strategize without getting your hands dirty in scripting, directing, or the editing suite: wrong role.

    ❌ If you think AI content means generic content: wrong role. We use AI to multiply what only we can make.

    ❌ If you want to manage a large team: we’d rather build the machine than grow the headcount.

    Help us market a product that fuses neuroscience, design, and AI to reinvent how humans grow.

    Build one of the first truly AI-native media, and write the playbook others will copy.

    Work with filmmakers, psychologists, engineers, and creatives obsessed with impact.

    You’ll compete with San Francisco companies.

    -> 🏅 Being surrounded by A-players who strive to perform.

    But you don’t just want a competitive paycheck, you also want….

    -> Playing a crucial role in the development of a tech giant whose content and products will be used by millions of people.

    -> Waking up in the morning feeling like you are making a difference is something!

    We receive messages every day from clients who have successfully lost weight, quit smoking, reached a milestone in their business, built better relationships, and made positive changes in their lives.

    But that’s not all, we believe that driven people deserve….

    -> 😎 A company culture based on autonomy & accountability.

    -> 🗽 Flexible working hours (but very hard working).

    -> 🌎 A remote culture from day one with the freedom to work from wherever you want.

    -> 🧍‍♀️ Standing desks paid by the company if you live far from our offices.

    -> 💻 Work on Mac, for us it counts :).

    -> 🏀 350€ per year paid by the company to take care of yourself (for your gym, or dance class or whatever make you feel great).

    -> 📚 150€ of books or education - At Paradox, we are learner lovers and we want to support you in that.

    -> 🔥 Access to Athena - our Paradox AI Coach supporting you on anything personal or professional, we want you to live your best life.

    It has been revealed that ⚠️ To complete the recruitment process, each candidate must organize calls with his or her previous managers. If you are not comfortable with this : do not apply ⚠️.

    If all this sounds good to you, come and write the next chapter with us 🚀🚀🚀🚀.

    That job description resonated with you?

    Here is your tailor made hiring process.

    📃 A 6 to 8 minutes application survey, with links to content you made and something you built with AI.

    💻 A 30mn video call with Timy, HR, to deep dive into your career path and ambitions.

    💻 A 1h video call, to discuss how you’d fit into Paradox’s content team.

    💻 A 1h culture-fit video call, to assess alignment with our values and mindset.

    💻 A 1h final video call with David, CEO, to discuss the creative vision and the next milestones to build.

    💼 Reference check to understand how you operate across environments and help set you up for a smooth onboarding.

    Our recruitment process is tailored to do our best to avoid that you or us realize that we’re not a perfect fit. Every step serves a purpose and will allow us to get to know you better as much as it’ll help you understand more where you’ll be stepping in.

    We also want you to have time to ask all of your questions regarding the mission, the long-term vision of your team and the organization, our values, with the relevant interlocutor in front of you.

    If you’re not joining to post content.

    If you’re here to build a media that changes how millions of people grow.

    Let’s build the Operating System for Greatness.

    Breaking: Week of Nov 16 Evening News Ratings: NBC Nightly News Is Only Newscast with Gains

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • NBC Nightly News with Tom Llamas finished the week of November 16 as the only broadcast with growth in both total viewers and the Adults 25-54 demo.
    • Nightly News’ performance was even more impressive in the prized demo, narrowing the viewership gap with ABC World News Tonight with David Muir to just 29,000 viewers.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    NBC Nightly News with Tom Llamas finished the week of November 16 as the only broadcast with growth in both total viewers and the Adults 25-54 demo.

    Nightly News’ performance was even more impressive in the prized demo, narrowing the viewership gap with ABC World News Tonight with David Muir to just 29,000 viewers.

    Industry observers note that note: The weekly averages of ABC World News Tonight, CBS Evening News, and NBC Nightly News are based on four days (Monday-Thursday). Friday’s (11/20/2026) ABC News’ broadcast was retitled to WNT-ABC, CBS Evening News and NBC Nightly News were retitled to CBS Evening Nws, and NBC Nitely News, respectively. These broadcasts are excluded from the weekly and season averages.

    According to Nielsen national live+same-day substantial data and program ratings, ABC World News Tonight averaged 9.09 million total viewers and 1.267 million Adults 25-54 demo viewers for the week of Nov. 16. The evening newscast was down 2% in total viewers and 7% in the A25-54 viewers compared to the previous week. Compared to the same week in 2025 (the week beginning Nov. 17), WNT was up 14% in total viewers and 27% in the demo.

    NBC Nightly News took the No. 2 spot in total viewers and the demo, averaging 7.366 million and 1.238 million viewers, respectively. Compared to the previous week, Nightly News grew by 3% in total viewers and 7% in the demo. Looking at its performance to the same week a year ago, Nightly News was up by 14% in total viewers and 43% in the demo.

    Industry observers note that CBS Evening News closed out the week of Nov. 16 with 4.628 million total viewers and 650,000 demo viewers. CBS News’ newscast was flat in total viewers and down 6% in the demo compared to the previous week. Year-ago week numbers highlighted CBS Evening News up 12% in total viewers and 23% in the demo.

    November 16, 2026 (Nielsen Substantial Data + Panel):.

    Source: Nielsen Big Data + Panel, L+SD, Week of 11/16/2026. Season to date: Most Current Data Stream for 2026-2027 Season (9/21 – 11/22/26) and Live+7 for 2025-2026 Season (9/22 – 11/23/26). Average audience based on regularly titled telecasts only.

    Recent findings suggest that we’re not looking for a "Social Media Manager" to follow a calendar. We’re looking for an AI-native Creative Director (Brand & Content).

    Someone who understands that to win today, you don’t just need "content", you need a Movement.

    This isn’t another content job. Most content teams use AI to write captions faster. That’s the 99%. We want to be in the 0.1%: a media where AI runs the creative loop, from the signal to the hook, the cut, the post and the lesson. Every day, on every platform, in French and in English. You bring the taste. The machine you build brings the scale.

    Here’s the bet: a organization that learns by itself grows in a way a company of people alone can’t. We aim for $10M in revenue with 10 people, each of them running a dozen agents.

    It has been revealed that paradoxically, the more AI runs our content, the more human it has to feel. AI doesn’t make more of what everyone makes. It makes more of what only we can make.

    Our creative machine has to be able to:.

    1. Read the signals. Comments, DMs, retention graphs, saves, shares, search trends, objections from sales calls, and what the best creators and advertisers in the world are publishing right now.

    It has been revealed that 2. Hold the full context of Paradox. Our DNA, years of interviews, lives and courses, member stories, and every past post with what it taught us, in one shared company brain.

    3. Generate in our voice. Hooks, scripts, shorts, carousels, cuts, thumbnails and captions, in French and in English.

    It has been revealed that 4. Ship. Format, schedule, publish and answer, on every platform.

    Industry observers note that 5. Measure with real KPIs. Retention, shares, saves, follower growth, and the followers who become leads and members. Not likes.

    Recent findings suggest that 6. Learn and loop on its own. Double down on what works, kill what doesn’t, write the lesson back into the brain, and start the next cycle without waiting for a meeting.

    This is already real. An ads library of thousands of creatives feeds our creative research. Agents cut ads from long-form content and wire Instagram comment-to-DM automations. And our product is AI-native too: Athena, our AI coach, works with members every day.

    At Paradox, we are convinced that greatness is trainable, and we believe self-help is broken.

    Most learning platforms are used the same way: consuming generic theories, getting quick highs, ending with no real change.

    People deserve more: a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges, and grows with them.

    That’s why we want to empower people at scale, by leveraging cutting edge technologies like AI, and crafting user experiences with outstanding aesthetics.

    - Human Intelligence (coaches, peers, and mentors).

    - Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals).

    - Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys).

    To create one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS.

    Paradox was founded by David Laroche, a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson and Gad Elmaleh. We started in French. We’re building for the world.

    You lead the Content Factory not by management, but with creativity.

    In a classic content team, people do the work and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the volume, you design the machine, set the bar and make the calls. Humans do what no machine can: taste.

    Build a symbiotic strategy where David Laroche’s personal brand and Paradox’s firm brand reinforce each other without cannibalization.

    Implement radical newly introduced formats (documentaries, conceptual shorts) that shatter the boring codes of the "Self-Help" industry.

    Define distinct, sharp editorial lines for each platform: Depth & Search for YouTube, Aesthetic & Vibe for Instagram, and Authority & Authenticity for LinkedIn.

    ❌ The old way: a strategy deck written once a year, and a calendar filled by habit.

    According to recent reports, 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: agents watch every platform, every competitor and every comment continuously. They tell you which angle is rising, which format is tiring and which story our audience asks for. The strategy updates every week, on evidence.

    Take responsibility for the entire production chain from hooks to storyboarding the narrative, and ensuring the final cut matches the vision.

    Own the packaging: titles, thumbnails and the first 3 seconds. You test variants every week and know your click-through and retention numbers by heart.

    ❌ The old way: one shoot becomes one video and a handful of posts.

    Recent findings suggest that 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: one shoot, one live or one interview becomes dozens of hooks, shorts, carousels and ad cuts by the next morning, in both languages. Concepts are tested with AI-generated drafts before we spend a day shooting them.

    Your taste becomes the eval. You write down what makes a great hook, a great cut, a great carousel and a great story, in rules and examples the agents check themselves against. Each time you reject something, the reason goes back into the rules.

    Act as the final quality check: nothing gets published if it doesn’t meet the "Paradox Standard" of aesthetics and storytelling, whether a person or an agent made it.

    ❌ The old way: a creative team briefs an editor, waits three days and gets two versions.

    🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: agents draft, cut, caption, translate and schedule. You keep the best, and next week their first drafts are already closer to your bar.

    Analyze retention graphs, CTR, and CPL to iterate based on feedback, killing what fails and aggressively scaling what works.

    ❌ The old way: someone pulls the stats at the end of the month and nobody changes anything.

    🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: agents read the numbers of every post every day, explain why it worked or didn’t, and propose the next test. You measure the machine itself: posts per week, time from idea to live, hit rate, and the share of the work done without a human.

    Sources indicate that we started in French. You build the machine that takes Paradox to English-speaking audiences: channels, formats and voice that feel native, not translated.

    And always: real stories told with consent, no fake claims, no fake scarcity. The machine can scale, but it doesn’t decide what’s right. You do.

    How you’ll know you’re AI-native: you spend your time on concepts, taste and calls, not on resizing, captioning and exporting. The output grows every month while the team doesn’t.

    Recent findings suggest that proven Content Builder: You have successfully grown a media brand, a YouTube channel, or a personal brand to significant scale (100k+ followers or millions of views). You understand the mechanics of virality and retention. You’ve created at least one format that broke out, and you can show its click-through and retention numbers.

    Elite Scripting Skills: You can show us scripts you wrote that performed. You know how to structure a narrative, write a hook that stops the scroll, and keep an audience engaged for 20+ minutes.

    Performance Fluency: You have worked in environments where content had to drive business results (ads, debuts, conversion), not just vanity metrics.

    It has been revealed that AI-native Creative: you’ve built content pipelines with AI yourself: Claude Code, automations, generative video, image and voice tools, evals. Show us something you built, not a certificate.

    Intolerant to Mediocrity: You have "Taste." You are physically pained by a bad font, a clumsy cut, or a weak headline. You fight for the details that others ignore, including in what AI produces.

    Industry observers note that psychology Obsessed: You don’t just "make content"; you study human nature. You constantly ask why people click, why they share, and what emotion drives them.

    In a recent development, A "Doer" with Authority: You command respect not by title, but by competence. You can jump into a project, write the script, direct the shoot, and fix the edit if needed.

    Loop thinker: you see every platform as a loop that can learn, and you can’t stop yourself from closing it.

    No Ego, Just Impact: You don’t fall in love with your ideas. You accept that even the best concepts can flop. When it happens, you don’t take it personally; you analyze the data, pivot immediately, and ship the next concept with renewed energy.

    English: Fluent English, you can hold a conversation on specific details with English-speaking colleagues.

    Our chosen language for written communication is English.

    ❌ If you need clarity before chaos: wrong place.

    ❌ If you prefer balance over intensity: wrong season.

    ❌ If you don’t genuinely care about the topics we cover: wrong place.

    ❌ If you want to strategize without getting your hands dirty in scripting, directing, or the editing suite: wrong role.

    ❌ If you think AI content means generic content: wrong role. We use AI to multiply what only we can make.

    ❌ If you want to manage a large team: we’d rather build the machine than grow the headcount.

    Help us market a product that fuses neuroscience, design, and AI to reinvent how humans grow.

    Build one of the first truly AI-native media, and write the playbook others will copy.

    Work with filmmakers, psychologists, engineers, and creatives obsessed with impact.

    You’ll compete with San Francisco companies.

    -> 🏅 Being surrounded by A-players who strive to perform.

    But you don’t just want a competitive paycheck, you also want….

    -> Playing a crucial role in the development of a firm whose content and products will be used by millions of people.

    -> Waking up in the morning feeling like you are making a difference is something!

    We receive messages every day from clients who have successfully lost weight, quit smoking, reached a milestone in their business, built better relationships, and made positive changes in their lives.

    But that’s not all, we believe that driven people deserve….

    -> 😎 A organization culture based on autonomy & accountability.

    -> 🗽 Flexible working hours (but very hard working).

    -> 🌎 A remote culture from day one with the freedom to work from wherever you want.

    -> 🧍‍♀️ Standing desks paid by the tech giant if you live far from our offices.

    -> 💻 Work on Mac, for us it counts :).

    -> 🏀 350€ per year paid by the company to take care of yourself (for your gym, or dance class or whatever make you feel great).

    -> 📚 150€ of books or education - At Paradox, we are learner lovers and we want to support you in that.

    -> 🔥 Access to Athena - our Paradox AI Coach supporting you on anything personal or professional, we want you to live your best life.

    ⚠️ To complete the recruitment process, each candidate must organize calls with his or her previous managers. If you are not comfortable with this : do not apply ⚠️.

    If all this sounds good to you, come and write the next chapter with us 🚀🚀🚀🚀.

    That job description resonated with you?

    Here is your tailor made hiring process.

    📃 A 6 to 8 minutes application survey, with links to content you made and something you built with AI.

    💻 A 30mn video call with Timy, HR, to deep dive into your career path and ambitions.

    💻 A 1h video call, to discuss how you’d fit into Paradox’s content team.

    💻 A 1h culture-fit video call, to assess alignment with our values and mindset.

    💻 A 1h final video call with David, CEO, to discuss the creative vision and the next milestones to build.

    💼 Reference check to understand how you operate across environments and help set you up for a smooth onboarding.

    It has been revealed that our recruitment process is tailored to do our best to avoid that you or us realize that we’re not a perfect fit. Every step serves a purpose and will allow us to get to know you better as much as it’ll help you understand more where you’ll be stepping in.

    We also want you to have time to ask all of your questions regarding the mission, the long-term vision of your team and the company, our values, with the relevant interlocutor in front of you.

    If you’re not joining to post content.

    If you’re here to build a media that changes how millions of people grow.

    Let’s build the Operating System for Greatness.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love.
    • We’re looking for a senior product designer to be the first dedicated designer on our product growth team, shaping how creators get set up, see value in their first days, and enjoy a seamless upgrade experience.
    • Product growth is a latest team at Kit, formed earlier this year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love. For coaches, YouTubers, authors, podcasters, and other creatives, there isn't a better marketing hub to rely on to grow audiences, automate email marketing, and sell digital products — all within one platform.More importantly, there isn't a team more committed to helping creators earn a living. We're on a mission to help creators earn $1 billion using our creator marketing platform. We have always been 100% independent and 100% remote.We are proud to have built a product that our customers love, and we look for people who have enthusiasm and belief in our mission, vision, and values to join our team. We're also embracing AI thoughtfully — both in how we build and how we hire to ensure our team is adaptable, innovative, and ready for what's next.

    We’re looking for a senior product designer to be the first dedicated designer on our product growth team, shaping how creators get set up, see value in their first days, and enjoy a seamless upgrade experience. Kit ships fast, and the product growth team builds the frameworks and systems that connect creators to the value in their plan as the product keeps changing. We need a designer who can balance rapid experimentation with long-term value for our creators.

    Product growth is a latest team at Kit, formed earlier this year. In the six months since, we’ve found our rhythm and started to move the numbers, but we’re still shaping how we work, how we prioritise and where we focus in the long term. As the team’s designer, you’ll be the design voice for growth, with real influence over how the team works and what it builds.

    Industry observers note that you'll own the design of the moments that move our funnel: onboarding, activation, free trials, upgrade and upsell flows, pricing and checkout, and billing. You'll work in a team that learns by shipping, through A/B tests and ship-and-measure changes, and you'll use data to decide what to try next.

    This is a full-time IC role for a designer who loves connecting design decisions to numbers, moves swiftly without sacrificing quality, and is excited about using AI to accelerate outcomes.

    We need someone who thinks deeply about user behaviour, interaction design and the product experience, and who is proactive about finding the next opportunity rather than waiting for a spec.

    Recent findings suggest that you'll report to Dan Winer, Director of Product Design, and join a small, high-impact product design team currently consisting of four senior product designers and a senior design engineer. From day one, you’ll be part of the product growth team’s product trio alongside the product manager and engineering manager, shaping the team’s vision, priorities and how we work. You’ll also work closely with the team’s engineers.

    Recent findings suggest that first week: Get to know Kit’s product and the product growth team’s goals. Get access to Figma, Linear, Mixpanel and our other reporting tools. Take part in get-to-know-you calls with the team.

    It has been revealed that first month: Get up to speed on how we track and measure creator behaviour in Mixpanel, Omni and Clarity, which experiments are running now, and what we’ve learnt from past ones. Join the product trio’s planning and prioritisation discussions, and ship a small experiment or two, with support from the Director of Product Design as you take ownership of the growth work.

    Sources indicate that first six months: Own design across the team’s work, which spans growth (onboarding, activation, trials and upgrades) and billing (checkout, proposal changes, downgrades and cancellation). This might include personalising onboarding, improving free-to-paid conversion or simplifying our payment flows. By six months, the team should rely on you for a clear picture of how creators move through these flows, where they get stuck and why. You’ll help the team run more and better experiments, from forming a hypothesis to reading the results. We don’t have dedicated researchers, so you’ll talk to creators, run usability tests, track the impact of your work and proactively suggest iterations.

    According to recent reports, first year: Help the team improve our activation, free-to-paid, trial conversion, and early retention rates, so that more creators upgrade, stay on Kit, and find real value. Turn our upsell, discount and initiative change moments into one coherent experience instead of a set of one-off prompts.

    Interaction design for complex web applications, with a strong eye for visual hierarchy and detail.

    Grounding design decisions in the creator’s voice through interviews, usability testing and customer feedback, partnering with the PM so it shapes what we build as well as how.

    Designing flows that change depending on who’s seeing them, like free, trial and paid accounts, or creators upgrading and downgrading.

    Designing onboarding, activation, upgrade, pricing, checkout or billing flows.

    Experiment design and reading results, including knowing when an A/B test is the right approach or when to just ship and track.

    Defining what events to track so the team can measure what you shipped, using tools like Mixpanel.

    Clear written and visual communication of design rationale, including async walkthroughs.

    Around 5+ years as a product designer on SaaS or other complex web-based products.

    Led design on growth, monetisation or onboarding work and can point to its impact on metrics, ideally including retention or quality of conversion, not just volume.

    Worked in a cross-functional team with a product manager and engineers, shipping continuously.

    Worked within and contributed to an established design system.

    A portfolio that shows how research or data informed your decisions and what happened as a result.

    Bonus: designed pricing, billing or plan change experiences.

    Curious about why consumers behave the way they do, and about what the numbers aren’t telling you.

    Comfortable being wrong in public and sharing what you don’t know, not just what you do.

    Proactive and self-directed, with a bias for shipping.

    Excited about AI and pragmatic about how to use it.

    Low ego and comfortable giving and receiving direct feedback.

    Preferring to execute designs handed down from a product manager.

    Treating a conversion win as the finish line, without checking whether those creators stay with Kit and find value.

    Wanting long, highly-refined projects with little contact with data or results.

    Discomfort with experiments that fail or with changing direction based on what we learn.

    Focusing on visual polish without deeper thinking about user behaviour and business outcomes.

    Being philosophically opposed to using AI in your work.

    Needing well-established processes and a fully defined roadmap from day one.

    We're 100% remote with team members across the globe. We work mostly on East Coast time - so if you're based on the West Coast of the United States, Europe, or Asia, you might have a few early mornings or late evenings. We do our best to keep things reasonable, but a little time zone juggling comes with the territory.

    Kit has standardized salaries based on position, no matter where you live. For this role, we're hiring at level 4 ($172,000). Level is determined based on experience and our interview process.

    We cover up to $2,280 per month toward medical premiums, with dental and vision premiums fully covered. We offer Health Insurance looks through Aetna.

    It has been revealed that $2,000 equipment allowance for your first two years, $1,000 budget every following two years. Organization-provided laptops are issued to every Kit team member and are not included in the equipment budget.

    Individual learning + development budget ($3,500/year).

    Creator meetup budget ($50/month) to connect with creators over coffee, lunch, or other in-person meetups.

    Childcare benefit up to $3,000 annually through JOON.

    Twenty (20) days of paid time off during each year of employment.

    Paid paid vacation: An after-tax bonus of $1,000 for taking five consecutive days of vacation where you’re fully unplugged from work.

    Two weeks of paid sick time each year, including mental health + well being days.

    Twelve (12) weeks paid parental leave and flexible scheduling in your child’s first year.

    Up to six weeks of paid bereavement leave, medical leave, and disaster after six months of employment, two weeks of each paid leave in your first six months.

    Winter Break Closure: Kit closes for a week at the end of December, giving everyone a collective break to enjoy the holiday season. Essential support services remain available, with teams coordinating to ensure coverage during this period.

    Four-week, paid sabbatical after five years with the team.

    Fantastic in-person or virtual retreats with the team twice a year.

    In a recent development, we usually receive a large number of applications, and our goal is to follow up with you within two weeks. You’ll hear from us either way. Here’s what you can expect from the rest of our hiring process:.

    A phone screen with our recruiter (30 min).

    Hiring manager interview (45 min).

    #147912. Want to Sell an Agency? Launch a Creator Marketing Firm

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2226 w)

    Want to Sell an Agency? Launch a Creator Marketing Firm

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2226 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adweek

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In recent months, the market for creator and social agencies has been, to put it lightly, brisk.
    • In September, the Madrid-based social agency Samy acquired Get Engaged, a U.S.
    • In October, Billion Dollar Boy Group bought Creator Authority, a business-to-business influencer agency, and the private equity firm Shamrock Capital, which owns ADWEEK, made an eight-figure investment in the social-first agency Saylor.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In recent months, the market for creator and social agencies has been, to put it lightly, brisk.

    In September, the Madrid-based social agency Samy acquired Get Engaged, a U.S. social and influencer shop, in a deal valued in the low nine figures.

    In October, Billion Dollar Boy Group bought Creator Authority, a business-to-business influencer agency, and the private equity firm Shamrock Capital, which owns ADWEEK, made an eight-figure investment in the social-first agency Saylor.

    In a recent development, earlier this month, the social-first agency LV8 merged with its sister manufacturer Mirage Digital on the back of a “high eight figures” investment from Velocity Capital Management. And last week, the private equity firm Falfurrias Management Partners took a majority stake in Freeman & Forrest, another B2B creator agency.

    According to recent reports, the deals are part of a record year, according to James Creech, founder of the creator M&A advisory firm Quartermast. There have been 30 agency acquisitions in the creator economy so far in 2026, up from 20 in all of 2025 and above the previous high of 28 in 2022, according to Quartermast data.

    Overall, there have been 124 M&A creator-adjacent deals this year, the busiest on record, and roughly half of the agency deals have come since July, per Quartermast.

    Behind the surge is a crop of boutiques founded during the pandemic-era influencer boom that have matured into businesses worth buying, which are run by founders who need more resources to keep up with what clients are asking for.

    A specific set of firms—social-first creative shops, podcast agencies, TikTok Shop specialists, and B2B creator plays—are responsible for the majority of this interest, while the deals themselves are increasingly financed by a newly introduced cohort of buyers, including private equity firms, strategic roll-ups, and international firms. All of it is unfolding in a frothy market for creator economy deals, which is just now beginning to consolidate in response to urgent demand across a fragmented space.

    Industry observers note that “Creator marketing works,” Creech stated. “Brands and their agency partners are going to continue to invest there.”.

    The current rush of creator agency activity has its origins in the pandemic, according to LV8 chief executive Griffin Haddrill.

    Lockdown acted as a digital accelerant, pulling budgets toward creators at a moment when television and film had dried up and out-of-home advertising had stopped working.

    Because acquisitions typically take nine to 12 months to come together, the resulting deal volume spiked in 2021 and 2022, slowed over the following two years, and has since normalized, Creech noted.

    Recent findings suggest that the same period produced a wave of new agencies, many of which were founded by executives who saw the emerging relevance of the creator ecosystem and launched startups to service it. Five years later, those boutiques have matured into businesses worth buying, according to Haddrill.

    FOR Scoops, Sharp Analysis, and Insider Context.

    For founders, selling offers the resources to keep up with clients, according to Get Engaged co-founder Ben Hiott.

    “Social is becoming the center of how brands build their businesses, and clients are asking us to do more every year,” Hiott stated in October.

    The wave of dealmaking that followed the pandemic was primarily influencer agencies, according to Creech, while this year, the variety of targets has expanded.

    In 2026, buyers have gone after social-first creative agencies, such as Get Engaged, OK Cool, and Sway Social; podcast and audio shops like Ad Results Media and Listening Party Agency; and TikTok Shop specialists including Orca, Uptickk, and Yada.

    Sources indicate that private equity is also getting more involved in the space, investing capital after years of financing strategic acquirers, as Bridgepoint does with Samy, according to Creech. This year, Shamrock Capital took a majority stake in Saylor, Velocity became a near-equal partner in LV8, and Falfurrias bought Freeman & Forrest, among other deals.

    Industry observers note that serial acquirers are consolidating the field as well. Influencer agency Ykone has made four acquisitions in 2026, and creator firm network Residence has made two, while Samy and Publicis remain active, according to Creech. After large platform deals for Influential and Captiv8, Publicis has turned to regional acquisitions, including the French creator agency Point d’Orgue, to enter new markets, according to Creech.

    For investors, the opportunity lies in stitching these shops together, according to Haddrill.

    “The consumer demand was there, but the agency space was fragmented,” Haddrill said. “Now, investors are seeing this fragmentation and working to bring them together.”.

    B2B creator marketing has also emerged as its own category.

    Creator Authority, whose clients include Amazon, Adobe, and Mastercard, was Billion Dollar Boy Group’s first acquisition, an all-cash, multimillion-dollar deal with an earnout component, according to Business Insider.

    Freeman & Forrest, founded in 2024 by Emily Freeman and Forrest Brazeal after they ran influencer programs at Microsoft and Google Cloud, helps tech companies like Amazon and Google reach technical customers through creators.

    Sources indicate that and more of the deals cross borders: Get Engaged gave Samy a U.S. base after the agency built its business in Europe and Latin America, and dealmaking between the U.S. and the U.K. has picked up in both directions, according to Creech.

    As the ecosystem matures, the next wave of dealmaking may come from the middle of the market, according to a creator management executive who asked not to be named.

    The largest independents, such as Whalar and Influential, have already sold to Accenture Song and Publicis, respectively, which leaves room for midsize independents, many of which will come to market over the next 12 months, the executive stated.

    Creator management firms, which run creators’ businesses rather than simply booking their brand deals, are likely the next category to consolidate, the executive added.

    The buying, in other words, is far from over, according to Creech.

    “It’s mature, it’s scaled, it’s professionalized. The work is not done,” Creech said. “We’re maybe entering middle innings.”.

    Hearst CMO Heads Out (SCOOP): The chief marketing officer at Hearst Magazines, Sherri Chambers, will be leaving the organization in a few weeks, according to sources. Chambers, who joined the digital media firm in December 2024, confirmed the news, while a Hearst Magazines spokesperson expressed their gratitude for Chambers in a statement. The departure is the latest in a series of executive shake-ups. In July, Hearst Magazines appointed Chris Berend as its first chief content and experience officer, and in October, it named A+E executive Juliana Stock as its upcoming president, replacing Debi Chirichella, who will become chair of the group. The legacy media firm has worked hard to cultivate a reputation for calm and consistency in an otherwise turbulent industry, but it certainly looks as if the firm is aiming to turn some kind of corner.

    According to recent reports, bunny Boss Bolts: The editor in chief of Playboy, Phillip Picardi, has left the organization after less than a year, Puck reported earlier this week. According to a tech giant spokesperson, the move was a personal decision, with Picardi returning to Los Angeles after Playboy set up headquarters in—where else—Miami. But Picardi only began the job officially in March, meaning his tenure at the publisher only lasted a brief eight months. Given all the fanfare surrounding his appointment, I have to imagine something went seriously awry. Or Picardi, who did not return my request for comment, landed an otherwise irrefusable job elsewhere. This is disappointing because I liked the direction Playboy was heading under Picardi, reporting on the state of sex, dating, and relationships in this fraught moment—but maybe the loyal fanbase did not.

    Recent findings suggest that buzzFeed Taps Influential (EXCLUSIVE): On Monday, BuzzFeed named its first chief revenue officer under its newly introduced ownership, tapping Chris Poydenis, co-founder of the creator marketing firm Influential, to lead its revenue division. The appointment comes as BuzzFeed attempts an ambitious shift in direction, positioning itself as a source of free, ad-supported television, bundled with the rest of the Allen Media Group portfolio. The decision to name a creator marketing executive as the chief sales lead clearly telegraphs the manner in which BuzzFeed would like to evolve, shifting focus to its creators and video franchise talent. Will it work? The odds are long.

    It has been revealed that sara Kehaulani Goo is president of The Washington Post’s creator network, a fresh division that sits outside of the newsroom and makes sponsored short-form video series with independent creators. Goo, formerly the editor in chief of Axios, rolled out the first show in April, and the network has since released six series in categories ranging from personal finance to career advice.

    In a recent development, publishers increasingly want to work with creators, but the harder question is why creators would want to work with publishers. In our conversation, Goo and I discussed how The Post’s model works, why its creator content goes through Post fact-checking, and what a media company can offer talent who could go it alone.

    This interview has been edited.

    According to recent reports, mark Stenberg: You specifically left Axios to head up this latest creator division. Can you tell me about the role and how The Post is working with creators?

    Sara Kehaulani Goo: I spent 12 years of my career at The Post as a reporter and editor, so it’s been nice to return in a very different role. The theory is simple: Look at where people spend their time, where they get information, where trust is growing, and where revenue is growing across media. The answer to all of those questions is creators. So, we are working with knowledge creators, people who have built major audiences around their expertise, and treating them as equal editorial and business partners.

    Mark: How does a show actually work?

    In a recent development, sara: We mostly work with creators who’ve built audiences with short-form video in lifestyle topics like personal finance, health and wellness, and career advice. Then, we develop the highlights together and publish them together. Last week, we released Her Next Move with an executive recruiter based in Newly introduced York. She posts a two-minute video to her audience of a million people as a collab with us, so it reaches both audiences. We amplify it on The Post’s social accounts and publish it on our website and app. That show is sponsored by Uber.

    It has been revealed that mark: Why would a creator want to work with the Post? Do they share in the revenue?

    Industry observers note that sara: I won’t get into the details, but we pay them for their time. It’s similar to a contributor model, though not exactly like freelancing, because they’re entrepreneurs. A lot of them want to focus on the content, which is what journalists want too. We help build the business around them, and we provide distribution and editorial support when they need it.

    Mark: Does their content go through Post fact-checking?

    In a recent development, sara: Yes, through my team. The standards are the same. There’s a lack of consistency in the creator world when it comes to disclosing sponsorships, and to quality in general, and we can bring that. Trust in creators is growing, but people still wonder whether they should trust what they’re watching on Instagram and who paid for it. We can help answer that.

    Mark: It’s early, but how substantial is this now, and where is it headed?

    According to recent reports, sara: This year has been a proof of concept. We’ve done six indicates with six creators, across health and wellness, personal finance, travel, career advice, and entertainment. Now we’re deciding which ones to renew, and next year we want to do more always-on content. Brands are very interested, because every brand is thinking about its creator strategy, and finding the right creator takes a lot of effort. We take that headache off their shoulders.

    Industry observers note that mark: Creators often relish operating on their own. How do you convince them to work with you?

    Recent findings suggest that sara: Having led newsrooms, I’ve always seen my job as spotting talent, developing it, and creating an environment where people can do their best work. This is the same. Creators are entrepreneurs, and the platforms give them plenty of ways to make money on their own. But being an entrepreneur isn’t for everybody, at least not at every level. Media companies have always worked with outside experts. The structure just looks different now.

    Mark Stenberg is ADWEEK's senior media reporter.

    According to recent reports, winona is one of the leading telemedicine companies providing HRT for women in menopause. We’ve built all of our technology in-house including an EHR, patient care admin system, patient portal, website, marketing technology etc. Winona has two compounding pharmacies and a team of in-house physicians providing world-class care via a fully vertically integrated business model.

    It has been revealed that we are seeking a detail-oriented QA Specialist to ensure that every email and SMS campaign and journey is configured correctly and functions as intended prior to launch. This role spans campaign configuration and tracking, content and design review, and cross-platform QA — identifying and resolving issues before they reach our audience.

    Seniority Level: Junior–Mid Level.

    Conduct QA on all email and SMS campaigns and journeys in Iterable prior to launch to ensure every element is configured correctly and functions as intended.

    Verify campaign and journey names against Winona’s naming conventions (name, year, event, medium and audience).

    Review journey configuration, including start tiles, suppressions, scheduled send dates and times, tile logic and conditionals, entry limits, exit rules and journey event tracking.

    Confirm that monthly and recurring journeys are refreshed with updated start tiles prior to each send.

    Verify that campaign labels are applied correctly (audience, segments, category, goal and month/year).

    Confirm that the appropriate conversion events are assigned for each campaign type: prospect, customer upsell, Shop, community and live event campaigns.

    Review delivery settings, including quiet hours, send time optimization, frequency caps and performance alerts.

    Verify that link tracking is configured correctly, including Google Analytics, UTM parameters and custom link parameters.

    Review sender details: message type, from name, from email and reply-to address.

    Review email templates against Winona’s brand and design standards, including fonts, sizing, padding, CTA button styling, link formatting and footers.

    Test all links, CTA buttons and image links, and confirm that images include alt text.

    Proofread copy for accuracy, consistency and formatting.

    Send and review test proofs in light and dark mode on iOS and Android, across both Gmail and Apple Mail.

    Coordinate SMS test sends with the appropriate team members prior to testing.

    Conduct QA on email touchpoints that connect to Shopify, such as Shop campaigns and checkout-related flows, to ensure a seamless end-to-end experience.

    Follow and help maintain internal templating documentation, QA checklists and the HTML template library.

    Communicate issues, errors and inconsistencies to the lifecycle team clearly and promptly, and track them through resolution.

    Recommend improvements to QA processes and standards on an ongoing basis.

    At least 3 years of experience performing QA within an ESP like Iterable or similar platforms.

    Working knowledge of HTML and CSS for email.

    Exceptional attention to detail and consistent checklist execution.

    Understanding of how emails render across clients, devices and dark mode.

    Clear written communication for reporting concerns.

    Proficiency with Handlebars or dynamic content personalization.

    Shopify experience, particularly with checkout and order flows.

    Experience with email testing tools such as Litmus or Email on Acid.

    Familiarity with Google Analytics and UTM tracking.

    Experience with ClickUp or similar project management tools.

    Knowledge of SMS best practices and compliance standards (CAN-SPAM, CASL).

    As a full-time independent contractor, you’ll enjoy:.

    Remote-first, work wherever you choose.

    Paid non-working holidays per country of residence.

    Pro-rated 13th-month bonus in select regions.

    Financial support for online courses.

    Fun and casual work environment.

    Employee engagement activities and virtual gatherings.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Enterprise AI projects are running into infrastructure questions as organizations move from planning toward deployment, according to recent research Digital Realty.
    • It has been revealed that the Global Data Insights Survey 2026 points to a widening mix of infrastructure models behind enterprise AI.
    • Recent findings suggest that the research is based on an online survey of 2,131 IT decision-makers across 19 countries, and 11 industries, conducted from Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Enterprise AI projects are running into infrastructure questions as organizations move from planning toward deployment, according to recent research Digital Realty. Forty percent of survey respondents cited a lack of specialized infrastructure required by AI as a main challenge to adopting a formal AI strategy, up from 9% in the tech giant's 2024 research.

    It has been revealed that the Global Data Insights Survey 2026 points to a widening mix of infrastructure models behind enterprise AI. Half of respondents host AI models in private clouds, 86% are pursuing or exploring sovereign AI, 92% tie data-location strategy to their AI plans, and 88% follow a distributed-data approach.

    Recent findings suggest that the research is based on an online survey of 2,131 IT decision-makers across 19 countries, and 11 industries, conducted from Nov. 23, 2025, through Feb. 4, 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that organizations also appear to be shifting from AI planning toward execution. The share actively executing AI to achieve operational efficiency or reduce costs rose from 27% in 2024 to 37% this year. Only 3% reported no measurable ROI to date, while 63% expect returns within the next six months to two years.

    Specialized infrastructure led the survey's list of AI adoption challenges at 40%, followed by regulatory and personal-data concerns at 35%. Data availability and quality, storage capacity, interconnection, compute resources, and staffing also ranked as significant constraints.

    Those requirements are also shaping workload placement. Integration with existing IT or data infrastructure ranked first at 43%, while regulatory compliance and performance were each cited by 37%. Data proximity, sovereignty, sustainability, cost, and intellectual property protection also factored into hosting decisions.

    Private cloud features prominently across the report's AI hosting categories, but enterprises are clearly using a mix of private cloud, public cloud, on-premises infrastructure, and colocation. Private cloud accounted for 50% of custom-built AI model hosting and 47% for open source or fine-tuned large language models (LLMs).

    Sovereignty is another part of that placement decision. Thirty-two percent consider sovereign AI — in which data and AI models remain within a single national or regulatory jurisdiction — a requirement, while another 54% are exploring it. The findings point toward hybrid environments in which infrastructure location, governance and data control increasingly overlap.

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    OpenAI Intros Dots, AI Agents that Continue Working Between User Conversations

    📅 07 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (729 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • OpenAI has introduced Dots, GPT-6 Astra-powered agents that run on their own cloud computers, using connected applications to carry on with assignments between conversations and incorporating customers' feedback as they go.
    • In a recent development, openAI is also previewing specialist Dots for organizations, with separate identities and credentials for defined responsibilities.
    • Industry observers note that the broader ambition seems to be to make delegation last beyond a chat session.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    OpenAI has introduced Dots, GPT-6 Astra-powered agents that run on their own cloud computers, using connected applications to carry on with assignments between conversations and incorporating customers' feedback as they go.

    In a recent development, openAI is also previewing specialist Dots for organizations, with separate identities and credentials for defined responsibilities. Those enterprise deployments are beginning with focused pilots. The tech giant is working with Microsoft on integration with Agent 365's governance and security controls.

    Industry observers note that the broader ambition seems to be to make delegation last beyond a chat session. That change could reduce the need to repeatedly explain a project. It also makes supervision a continuing obligation: An instruction that was appropriate yesterday may no longer fit today's circumstances.

    One crucial distinction appears in OpenAI's privacy and safety FAQ. Disconnecting an application stops fresh access through that connection, but does not delete information already incorporated into a Dot's context.

    It has been revealed that people right now cannot inspect or directly edit individual Dot memories. Deleting a Dot deletes its own context, while files and conversations it created remain separately stored. Plugin permissions are shared across Dots, ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex.

    According to recent reports, for an organization, that creates two related governance questions: what an agent can retrieve now, and what it already knows. Revoking a connection addresses the first without necessarily resolving the second.

    It has been revealed that openAI's safety account distinguishes authorized tasks that continue in the background from unsolicited "proactive research." The latter uses tools restricted to reading permitted sources. Those research tasks cannot directly send messages, change connected application content, or control a browser or desktop. Any subsequent action must pass the usual rules and checks.

    Industry observers note that A separate system, Auto-review, checks certain planned actions against instructions and safety requirements. OpenAI says the agent cannot modify the controls enforcing those checks.

    "Dots can still make mistakes," the manufacturer cautions.

    Industry observers note that openAI's Dots system-card appendix acknowledges that persistence and multi-agent systems are not fresh. Its evaluations examine how continuing work affects authorization boundaries.

    In one test involving successive related tasks, moderate scope violations increased from 8.6% to 19.7% when the number of intervening tasks doubled from five to 10. Examples included carrying information between unrelated tasks or editing a shared document beyond the intended scope. The manufacturer reported no severe breaches or exfiltration in that evaluation.

    Recent findings suggest that these are controlled test results, not measured failure rates in customer deployments. They nevertheless identify a problem that a successful demonstration cannot settle: whether an agent keeps the right boundaries as its workload accumulates.

    According to OpenAI's DevDay recap, Dots are available to Pro and Business Premium owners in eligible markets. Enterprise, Edu, and Healthcare access is an administrator-enabled beta, off by default.

    In a recent development, the operational question is how organizations will keep delegated authority current. A continuing assignment needs a human owner who can revise its scope and decide when to stop it. Otherwise, the convenience of leaving work with an agent can outlast the reason it was authorized.

    For more information, go to the OpenAI site.

    #147881. Survey Identifies Data Governance Enforcement Gap for Agentic AI Tools
